places.name: Sunrise Inc. (Bandai Namco Filmworks) Studio 1
places.connection: Primary animation studio responsible for the production of the 1998 TV series 'Cowboy Bebop'.

places.name: Kowloon Walled City Park (Former Site of Kowloon Walled City)
places.connection: Widely cited as a major visual inspiration for the densely packed, vertical, and often chaotic urban environments seen on various planets (e.g., Mars, Ganymede) in the series.

places.name: Times Square
places.connection: Inspired the bustling, neon-lit, futuristic commercial districts with a distinct Western feel depicted in many of the series' urban settings.

places.name: French Quarter (Jackson Square Area)
places.connection: Strong influence on the series' iconic jazz soundtrack, bluesy atmosphere, and some architectural elements of more rustic or historic parts of cities.

places.name: Grand Central Terminal
places.connection: A common inspiration for grand, ornate, futuristic transportation hubs and public spaces in science fiction, reflected in some of the series' large interior settings.

places.name: Djemaa el-Fna and Souks
places.connection: The bustling, labyrinthine markets and vibrant street life, particularly on Tijuana (Mars) in Episode 1 'Asteroid Blues', draw heavily from traditional North African souks.

places.name: Shibuya Crossing
places.connection: Represents the hyper-urban, neon-lit, and densely populated futuristic cityscapes seen throughout the series, a common visual reference for modern anime. Also a general anime pilgrimage hotspot.

places.name: The Bund (Peace Hotel Area)
places.connection: The blend of colonial and futuristic architecture along waterfronts, especially at night, aligns with some of the more developed port cities in the series.

places.name: Rialto Bridge (Venice Canals)
places.connection: The unique water-based urban structure and historical European charm could have inspired some of the more distinct or partially submerged cities, particularly on Venus.

places.name: Las Vegas Strip (Bellagio Fountains)
places.connection: The flashy, entertainment-focused, and sometimes decadent atmosphere of gambling planets and nightlife districts in the series.

places.name: Roy's Motel & Cafe
places.connection: An iconic example of an American desert roadside stop, providing visual inspiration for the truck stop and desolate highway settings in Episode 7 'Heavy Metal Queen'.

places.name: Notre Dame Cathedral
places.connection: Representative of the grand, imposing Neo-Gothic architectural style used for significant buildings like the Syndicate headquarters in the series.
